content:
The 2025 Outlook for the European Technology Ecosystem

According to data from the Europe & Turkey Technology and Investment Report, Europe-based technology companies received a total of 72 billion euros in investment in 2025. This figure marks the second-highest investment volume recorded over the past three years. While more than 3,740 deals were closed throughout the year, investor interest was observed to be shifting particularly toward infrastructure technologies that support economic resilience, industrial competitiveness, and long-term growth.

Artificial intelligence (AI), data center infrastructure, and renewable energy solutions were the leading sectors in investment rounds. The increase in strategic and infrastructure-focused investments signals that the ecosystem is maturing.

The 25 Technology Companies with the Highest Investment

The companies and their areas of operation, ranked by the amount of funding they received in 2025, are listed below:

  • CityFibre (UK) – 2.3 Billion Pounds: Fiber-to-the-premises (FTTP) infrastructure provider.
  • Propel Finance (UK) – 1.5 Billion Pounds: Asset and vehicle financing solutions for businesses.
  • Mistral AI (France) – 1.7 Billion Euros: Open-source large language models (LLMs) and generative AI tools.
  • Nscale (UK) – $1.53 billion: High-performance GPU-powered AI cloud and data center infrastructure.
  • Ubisoft (France) – 1.16 Billion Euros: Game development and digital entertainment publishing.
  • Bending Spoons (Italy) – 1.1 Billion Euros: Digital product development and software scaling platform.
  • EcoDataCenter (Sweden) – 1.05 Billion Euros: Sustainable and high-performance data centers.
  • Finn (Germany) – 1 Billion Euro: Subscription-based vehicle ownership platform.
  • NXP Semiconductors (Netherlands) – 1 Billion Euro: Semiconductor manufacturing focused on the automotive and IoT sectors.
  • Grammarly (Ukraine) – $1 billion: AI-powered writing assistant and communication platform.
  • Nebius (Netherlands) – $1 Billion: Full-stack AI cloud infrastructure and GPU clusters.
  • Nokia (Finland) – $1 billion: Network infrastructure and telecommunications technologies (with a focus on AI integration).
  • Enpal (Germany) – 810 Million Euros: Solar energy and integrated home energy management solutions.
  • Your.World (Netherlands) – 800 Million Euros: Online services and digital transformation solutions.
  • Oura (Finland) – $900 million: Smart health tracking ring and biometric data analytics.
  • Helsing (Germany) – 600 million euros: AI-based software solutions for the defense industry.
  • IONITY (Germany) – 600 Million Euros: High-power electric vehicle charging network.
  • Capital on Tap (United Kingdom) – 500 Million Pounds: A credit and financing platform for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).
  • Isomorphic Labs (UK) – $600 million: AI models for drug discovery.
  • Bees & Bears (Germany) – 505 Million Euros: An embedded finance platform for renewable energy products.
  • Brevo (France) – 500 Million Euros: CRM and multichannel marketing automation.
  • Elvy (Sweden) – 500 Million Euros: Energy management and optimization software.
  • Lovable (Sweden) – 470 Million Euros: A no-code application development platform powered by natural language processing.
  • Ferovinum (UK) – 400 Million Pounds: Supply chain financing for the wine and beverage industry.
  • Electra (France) – 433 million euros: Operation of fast-charging stations for electric vehicles.
